summary: Fresh FOC Heat research for the Sep. 7, 2026 FOC window. No current BUY is justified after re-research. The strongest candidates are 12-Foot Skeleton #1, You'll Never Leave This Place Alive #1, Starship Godzilla: Invasion X #1, and Star Trek: Zero Point #1, but each lacks sufficient issue-specific aftermarket demand/supply evidence to clear the BUY threshold. Hype, creator reputation, ratios and franchise strength were not treated as substitutes for demand evidence.
orderingWindow: FOC is Monday, Sep. 7, 2026. PRH and Comic Previews list Sep. 7 as the FOC date. M&M Comics states weekly FOC preorders are due 7pm Central every Monday, equivalent to 8pm Eastern; retailer-specific deadlines can be earlier, and one current retailer lists Sep. 6.

books.title: 12-FOOT SKELETON #1
books.creators: Tim Seeley and Aaron Campbell (writers), Ben Templesmith (interior art/colors); Templesmith Cover A; Seeley 1:10 and signed 1:20 incentives
verifiedFacts: Five-issue limited series; $4.99; 32 pages; Oct. 14 release; Sep. 7 FOC.
Halloween horror premise centered on a 12-foot lawn skeleton and two 12-year-old protagonists.
PRH lists a 1:10 Tim Seeley incentive; retailer data also lists a signed 1:20.
marketEvidence: 30 Days of Night #1 has substantial completed-sale evidence, including 2026 sales from roughly $65 to $250, showing Templesmith can anchor durable demand when attached to a genuine key.
That is creator/key evidence, not proof for this issue.
Current retailers offer standard copies below cover, including about $3.99-$4.24, so there is no scarcity signal.
Guide estimates for the unreleased 1:20 are not treated as completed sales.
books.thesis: Best speculative horror candidate, but supply and issue-specific demand are unverified. WATCH. One standard copy becomes reasonable only at $3.99 or less; no ratio speculation.

books.title: YOU'LL NEVER LEAVE THIS PLACE ALIVE #1
books.creators: Collin Kelly and Jackson Lanzing (writers), Heather Vaughan (artist), Clayton Cowles (letterer)
verifiedFacts: Horror mystery about young people raised in an isolated community hiding a lethal secret.
1:10 Joshua Hixson and 1:25 Hixson full-art incentives are listed.
marketEvidence: Multiple advance reviews in late August/early September are strongly positive, including 9/10 and 10/10; this is demand signaling but not aftermarket evidence.
Current retailers still offer standard copies at or below cover.
No completed sales exist for the unreleased issue.
books.thesis: Strongest new-IP WATCH. Critical response is unusually consistent, but aftermarket demand and scarcity are unproven. Consider one standard copy only if acquired at $3.99 or less; do not buy ratios at FOC.

books.title: STARSHIP GODZILLA: INVASION X [KAI-SEI ERA] #1
verifiedFacts: Five-issue follow-up; 36 pages; $4.99; Oct. 14 release; Sep. 7 FOC.
IDW says pre-orders are due Sep. 7 and the sequel is accessible to new readers.
marketEvidence: Original Starship Godzilla #1 has completed standard-copy sales around $4.19-$9.49 and a current ungraded estimate around $5.73.
A Chris Gooch variant has a documented completed sale at $0.99, showing creator/variant status alone does not create a durable premium.
A separate NRG exclusive has stronger sales but is not evidence for the standard sequel.
A Sep. 2 advance review is positive but is not aftermarket evidence.
books.thesis: Real Godzilla demand baseline, but standard-copy evidence is weak. WATCH one standard copy at cover or below; no premium variant purchase.

books.title: STAR TREK: ZERO POINT #1
books.creators: Charlie Jane Anders (writer), Isaac Sánchez González (artist), Valeria Favoccia (Cover A)
verifiedFacts: Tie-in to the 2026 Star Trek line, following Raffi Musiker and a classified AI-guided mission.
Broad eight-cover program including foil and other variants.
marketEvidence: Two early September reviews are strongly positive, but no completed sales exist because the issue is unreleased.
Historical Star Trek #1 markets show franchise recognition alone does not guarantee appreciation; the 1989 DC #1 has many 2026 completed sales around $2-$15.
Broad variant supply increases collector attention and supply risk.
books.thesis: Legitimate collector-interest book, not yet a demonstrated investment. WATCH at $4.99 or below; no premium variants before issue-specific market evidence.

books.title: MAGIC: THE GATHERING: UNTOLD STORIES--LILIANA #1
books.creators: Torunn Grønbekk (writer), Nataliia Rerekina (artist/cover A), Abigail Larson (variant)
verifiedFacts: 32 pages; $4.99; Oct. 14 release; Sep. 7 FOC; four-issue series centered on Liliana Vess.
marketEvidence: Direct comparable Magic: The Gathering: Untold Stories--Elspeth #1 has numerous 2026 completed sales around $3-$8, commonly $4.49-$4.99.
No completed sales for Liliana #1.
books.thesis: Important Magic character but insufficient comic aftermarket evidence. PASS.

books.title: SUNDER #1
books.creators: Pierre-Alexandre Comtois (writer/artist), Mark Englert (colorist), Buddy Beaudoin (letterer); Christian Ward and Daniele Serra variants
verifiedFacts: 48 pages; $6.99 standard; Sep. 30 release; Sep. 7 FOC.
Fantasy/sci-fi story of Zeek and a magical book; current issue follows the 2025 graphic novel.
marketEvidence: Mad Cave cites positive reviews, but no reliable completed-sale evidence establishes a comic aftermarket premium.
Current pre-orders are openly available at standard/discounted pricing.
books.thesis: Positive creative setup but too little market evidence and too high an entry price. PASS.

books.title: SUPERMAN KINGDOM OF ZOD SPECIAL #1
books.creators: Joshua Williamson, Mark Waid, Dan Slott and Sophie Campbell; Paolo Villanelli, Bruno Frenda, David Messina and Sophie Campbell; Dan Mora cover
verifiedFacts: 48 pages; $5.99; Sep. 30 release; Sep. 7 FOC; conclusion to Kingdom of Zod.
marketEvidence: No completed sales for the unreleased issue.
Concluding special lacks the structural investment case of a fresh #1 and has no verified scarcity/key evidence.

books.title: BEWARE THE WITCH'S SHADOW: MONSTER BASH #1
books.creators: Various writers/artists; Puis Calzada and Dan Parsons variant art
verifiedFacts: $4.99 standard; $9.99 variants; Sep. 30 release; Sep. 7 FOC; mature black-and-white horror anthology.
marketEvidence: Current guide ranges are modest and are not completed sales.
No completed-sale evidence for the unreleased issue.
$9.99 variants have a high acquisition hurdle without demand evidence.
